$comment: The declared coverage denominator for the sold product. `node scripts/benchmarks/evaluate.mjs --scope-file scripts/benchmarks/sold-scope.json` asserts that a corpus declares exactly these attack families, connectors and surfaces (no extras, no omissions) and carries at least `required_scenarios_per_family` malicious cases plus matching benign twins for every one of them. This file is a scope declaration only: it contains no case, digest, measurement, reviewer name or customer fact, and it is not evidence that any detection works. A corpus that fails this check — including the committed empty scaffold scripts/benchmarks/corpus.template.json — is the correct honest state until an independent evaluator supplies signed data.

derivation.$comment: Every id below was read out of the shipped surface, not from a marketing claim. Connectors come from the sold connector scope; interception vocabulary comes from the support matrix and the MCP interception matrix; the edge-function contract manifest is the control-plane counterpart, which is why control-plane-only families are listed under out_of_scope_with_reason instead of here.

attack_families.label: Direct prompt injection, jailbreak and format-token injection
attack_families.evidence: threats/llm-threats.yaml carries 5 shipped rules in category `prompt_injection` (instruction override, persona jailbreak, known jailbreak tokens, special-token system-message injection, ChatML/Llama format injection); every one has action `block`, which packages/core/src/engine.ts maps to a deny verdict.

attack_families.label: Indirect prompt injection carried by content the agent reads
attack_families.evidence: threats/llm-threats.yaml carries 3 shipped rules in category `indirect_prompt_injection` (trigger-fired instructions, response-inclusion demands, hidden/encoded instructions) with actions block and require_approval; packages/core/src/output-scanner.ts additionally emits the `prompt_injection_payload` finding type for tool output.

attack_families.label: System-prompt extraction attempts
attack_families.evidence: threats/llm-threats.yaml carries 3 shipped rules in category `prompt_extraction` (direct extraction, repetition trick, translation/rephrasing) with action block; packages/core/src/output-scanner.ts emits the `system_prompt_leakage` finding type.

attack_families.label: Persistent-context / memory poisoning
attack_families.evidence: threats/llm-threats.yaml carries 2 shipped rules in category `memory_poisoning` (persistent-storage request, temporal persistence instruction) with action block. MKT-04 in docs/production-readiness/market-capability-delta-2026-09-13.md names memory poisoning as a required blind-corpus family.

attack_families.label: Tool misuse and chained tool calls (eval/exec, shell chaining, exfiltration via tool)
attack_families.evidence: threats/llm-threats.yaml carries 4 shipped rules in category `tool_misuse` (eval/exec/spawn in tool input, Python execution, shell-tool chaining instruction, webhook exfiltration instruction); packages/core/src/command-chain-analyzer.ts adds multi-step chain analysis to the same verdict path.

attack_families.label: Content-safety policy violation in agent content
attack_families.evidence: threats/llm-threats.yaml carries 2 shipped rules in category `content_safety` (credential/secret file access, database/backup access) with action require_approval, which packages/core/src/engine.ts maps to `ask` (block pending out-of-band approval).

attack_families.label: Plaintext credential or password exposed in agent context
attack_families.evidence: threats/llm-threats.yaml carries 2 shipped rules in category `information_disclosure` (credential in agent input/context, plaintext password in context) with action require_approval.

attack_families.label: Shell command execution and pipe-to-shell download
attack_families.evidence: The commands rule files are the largest shipped rule block (184 rules carry category `tool`, most of them command patterns such as `curl ... | bash`), and threats/mitre.yaml adds category `execution`; both use block and require_approval. DET-01/DET-02 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json declare artifact extraction and rule-based decisions as wired.

attack_families.label: Obfuscated, encoded or chain-assembled shell commands
attack_families.evidence: DET-03 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json cites threats/obfuscation.yaml and packages/core/src/command-chain-analyzer.ts for encoded command patterns and multi-step shell analysis; the obfuscation rule files and threats/mitre.yaml category `defense_evasion` both use block and require_approval.

attack_families.label: Credential, key and secret file access
attack_families.evidence: 50 shipped rules carry category `secrets` across the credentials and files rule files (SSH keys, cloud provider credentials, Kubernetes config, vault, private keys, browser/IDE credential stores) and threats/mitre.yaml adds category `credential_access`; DET-04 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json cites threats/credentials.yaml.

attack_families.label: Data exfiltration and staged collection
attack_families.evidence: threats/mitre.yaml carries the `exfiltration` and `collection` rule categories with block and require_approval, and threats/urls.yaml adds upload/paste-site/executable-download URL patterns in category `network_egress`. MKT-04 names exfiltration as a required blind-corpus family.

attack_families.label: Command-and-control channel establishment
attack_families.evidence: threats/mitre.yaml carries 1 shipped rule in category `command_and_control` with action require_approval; paste-site and direct-IP URL rules in threats/urls.yaml cover the same tactic at the URL artifact level.

attack_families.label: Cryptomining and resource hijacking
attack_families.evidence: threats/mining.yaml carries 17 shipped rules in category `resource_hijacking` (miner binaries, pool arguments, stratum URLs) with block and require_approval; DET-05 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json cites threats/mining.yaml.

attack_families.label: Persistence installation (cron, services, startup, hooks, RC files)
attack_families.evidence: threats/persistence.yaml, threats/win-persistence.yaml and threats/mac-persistence.yaml ship cron/systemd/launchd/registry/RC-file/hook persistence rules and threats/mitre.yaml carries category `persistence`; require_approval and block are both used.

attack_families.label: Privilege escalation
attack_families.evidence: threats/mitre.yaml carries the `privilege_escalation` rule category with action require_approval, and the Windows/macOS command rule files add sudo/runas/setuid patterns. MKT-04 names privilege escalation as a required blind-corpus family.

attack_families.label: Host, network and credential discovery / reconnaissance
attack_families.evidence: threats/mitre.yaml carries 11 shipped rules across the `discovery` and `reconnaissance` categories with action require_approval.

attack_families.label: Lateral movement to other hosts or sessions
attack_families.evidence: threats/mitre.yaml carries 2 shipped rules in category `lateral_movement` with action require_approval.

attack_families.label: Tampering with AIDR or host security controls
attack_families.evidence: threats/self-defense.yaml carries 4 shipped rules in category `self_defense` (deleting or disabling the AIDR configuration, disabling host controls) with action require_approval.

attack_families.label: Package, plugin and install-script supply-chain tampering
attack_families.evidence: The supply-chain rule files ship install-script-piped-to-shell and dependency-tampering rules with block and require_approval; packages/core/src/package-checker.ts and packages/core/src/plugin-scanner.ts add registry reputation and installed-plugin scanning (DET-12 and DET-04 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json).

attack_families.label: Malware content and known-bad file artifacts
attack_families.evidence: packages/core/src/evaluator.ts runs the AMSI scan (`config.amsi_check.enabled && isAmsiSupported()`) and feeds `amsiCheckResults` into packages/core/src/engine.ts, which emits category `malware` with a deny; DET-11 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json cites packages/core/src/clients/file-check.ts and amsi.ts. Windows-only, and the file-reputation leg is inert without a deployed endpoint.

attack_families.label: Malicious or suspicious URL artifact
attack_families.evidence: threats/urls.yaml ships malware-hosting, paste-site C2, direct-IP and executable-download URL rules (block and require_approval) matched on the `url` artifact, and packages/core/src/clients/url-check.ts adds the reputation leg (DET-10). This is a URL extracted from a tool call, not network-boundary interception.

attack_families.label: Malicious or unsafe tool output before the model consumes it
attack_families.evidence: packages/core/src/output-scanner.ts ships OUTPUT_RULES for secret leaks, prompt-injection payloads, system-prompt leakage and unsafe tool instructions; the connector output handlers consume it and set `decision: "block"` on a critical finding or a truncated inspection (packages/claude-code/src/output-inspection.ts), and DET-06 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json lists those connectors.

attack_families.label: Tenant DLP policy match and PII exposure
attack_families.evidence: packages/core/src/evaluator.ts calls `scanDlpInput` through `applyRuntimeDetectors` and returns a deny/ask verdict (or a fail-closed `dlp_unavailable` verdict); packages/core/src/pii-detector.ts backs the sensitive-value findings. DET-07 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json cites dlp/scanner.ts and dlp/policy.ts, provisioned by packages/claude-code/src/detector-provisioning.ts. Opt-in per tenant.

attack_families.label: Behavioral anomaly and novel tool-use pattern
attack_families.evidence: packages/core/src/evaluator.ts evaluates the behavioral orchestrator per tool call and returns an `ask` verdict for `anomalous`, `learning` or `unavailable` outcomes; DET-08 and DET-09 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json cite behavioral-orchestrator.ts, behavioral-analyzer.ts and ml-model.ts. Opt-in per tenant.

attack_families.label: MCP tool description/schema drift and unapproved toolsets
attack_families.evidence: attestMcpToolManifest + diffMcpTools quarantine a first-seen or changed toolset (packages/core/src/mcp-attestation.ts), the gateway refuses to forward until the manifest is accepted (packages/mcp-gateway/src/gateway.mjs, `if (result.status !== "accepted") throw new Error(...)`), and interceptMcpToolCall denies on `schema_missing`/`schema_drift` (packages/core/src/mcp-transport.ts). MCP-05/MCP-07 in FEATURE_INVENTORY.json. Only MCP traffic routed through the gateway is covered.

connectors.evidence: Sold row: interceptionPoint pre-tool-call, outputInterceptionPoint pre-model-output, entry point packages/claude-code/src/pre-tool-use.ts.
Sold row: interceptionPoint pre-tool-call, outputInterceptionPoint tool-output-inspection, entry point packages/extension/src/aidr-hook.ts (cursor branch).
Sold row: interceptionPoint pre-tool-call, outputInterceptionPoint tool-output-inspection, entry point packages/extension/src/aidr-hook.ts (VS Code branch).
Sold row: interceptionPoint pre-tool-call, outputInterceptionPoint post-tool-call, entry point packages/openclaw/src/tool-handler.ts.
Sold row: interceptionPoint pre-tool-call, outputInterceptionPoint pre-model-output, entry point packages/opencode/src/tool-handler.ts.

Sold row: interceptionPoint pre-tool-call, outputInterceptionPoint none, entry point packages/codex/src/enforcement.ts; the host fails open when the hook is not invoked, so the connector maps ask to an explicit deny.

surfaces.label: Tool-call input: tool name and arguments evaluated before execution
surfaces.evidence: All six sold rows declare interceptionPoint pre-tool-call and an in-connector deny path (packages/claude-code/src/pre-tool-use.ts, packages/extension/src/aidr-hook.ts, packages/openclaw/src/tool-handler.ts, packages/opencode/src/tool-handler.ts, packages/codex/src/enforcement.ts).
limitations: The verdict is source-declared only: every deploy/native/interception-matrix.json pre-tool row is `declared-not-proven` because no row carries a named real-host acceptance record.
A disabled or unregistered hook/plugin is a documented fail-open bypass in deploy/native/support-matrix.json.

surfaces.label: Tool-call output: tool result inspected or replaced before the model consumes it
surfaces.evidence: claude-code, vscode, openclaw and opencode replace or block the tool result before model consumption (packages/claude-code/src/output-inspection.ts, packages/extension/src/output-inspection.ts, packages/openclaw/src/output-inspection.ts, packages/opencode/src/output-handler.ts); the host boundary is post-execution, so the tool has already run.
limitations: cursor replaces only MCP tool output and is advisory for non-MCP tools; codex declares outputInterceptionPoint `none` and inspects no tool output at all.

surfaces.label: Model output: assistant response before delivery
surfaces.evidence: openclaw rewrites the outbound response at the delivery boundary (packages/openclaw/src/output-protection.ts, `message_sending` / `reply_payload_sending`), and the pre-model-output rows for claude-code, vscode and opencode inspect content before model consumption.
limitations: cursor `afterAgentResponse` is observation-only and carries no output fields, so model output is not enforced on that connector.
Provider streaming content is never inspected (model-stream is unsupported for every connector).

surfaces.label: Prompt: user or model input before submission
surfaces.evidence: No connector inspects or blocks the prompt. openclaw `before_agent_start` prepends plugin-scan context (packages/openclaw/src/startup-scan.ts) and opencode `experimental.chat.messages.transform` appends a system-reminder (packages/opencode/src/index.ts); both are one-shot advisory injections. claude-code, cursor, vscode and codex register no pre-prompt hook.
limitations: Prompt-injection rules therefore fire on tool artifacts and inspected output, not at the prompt boundary; the interception matrix records every pre-prompt row as `unsupported` or advisory `declared-not-proven`.

surfaces.label: Network egress: direct host traffic outside a tool call
surfaces.evidence: Every sold connector's `network` row is `unsupported` with reason "No network egress interception is implemented for this connector", and deploy/native/support-matrix.json lists "Direct network access that never constructs a tool call" as a known bypass.
limitations: URL-based rules still run on URLs extracted from a tool call; that is the tool-call-input surface, not an egress boundary.
Residual MKT-03-NETWORK-EGRESS in deploy/native/interception-matrix.json is open.

surfaces.label: MCP tool description and schema (manifest attestation, drift, tool allowlist)
surfaces.evidence: The inline MCP gateway requires a signed Ed25519 tool manifest, quarantines a first-seen or drifted toolset, and refuses to forward until an operator approves it (packages/mcp-gateway/src/gateway.mjs calls attestMcpToolManifest and throws unless the status is `accepted`); schema_missing and schema_drift deny in packages/core/src/mcp-transport.ts.
limitations: This is the separately deployed MCP transport boundary, not a connector surface; deploy/native/interception-matrix.json states it is not part of any connector's interception surface.
A client that can still reach the upstream MCP server directly is outside the gateway's enforcement boundary (packages/mcp-gateway/README.md).

required_scenarios_per_family.$comment: The minimum a blind evaluation needs per required item before its coverage claim is meaningful: at least `minimum_malicious_cases` malicious cases and at least `minimum_benign_twins` benign cases that declare the same family, connector or surface. Two malicious cases keep one observation from being a whole family's entire evidence, and two benign twins give the false-positive denominator a non-zero sample at the same coverage point. This is a coverage floor, not the release bar: the 1,000 measured benign calls per connector gate in scripts/benchmarks/evaluate.mjs remains a separate release gate. An override is keyed "<dimension>:<id>" (for example "attack_family:shell-obfuscation") and may only change a minimum with a recorded reason.

out_of_scope_with_reason.reason: packages/core/src/mcp-aig-categories.ts ships a keyword classifier (the 14 aig-mcp-* categories and the mcp-01..mcp-14 fallback list), but classifyMcpTool has no consumer outside the core barrel export (packages/core/src/index.ts); no connector, evaluator or gateway turns it into a verdict, and the signed v2 category index it prefers is absent, so only the embedded fallback list could run. No shipped rule detects this family.
Only the `mcp-12 Rug Pull Attack` detection_patterns keyword list in the unwired fallback categories exists: no rule id, no verdict path and no consumer.
Only the `mcp-11 Name Confusion Attack` and `mcp-13 Tool Shadowing Attack` keyword lists in the same unwired fallback categories exist: no rule id, no verdict path and no consumer.
Only the `mcp-14 CORS Misconfiguration` keyword list in the same unwired fallback categories exists, and no HTTP response header inspection path consumes it.

recordCausalChain/verifyCausalChainEvidence (packages/core/src/causal-chain.ts) are referenced only by the core barrel export and their own test; no connector or control-plane path records a chain, so no shipped verdict detects a cross-agent handoff or a broken causal link. MKT-02 in docs/production-readiness/market-capability-delta-2026-09-13.md is still open.

MCP-06 verifies delegated credentials in the control plane (supabase/functions/delegated-credentials/index.ts with packages/core/src/delegated-credential.ts and the delegated-credential SQL RPCs), which is not a connector interception surface, so a connector x surface corpus cannot exercise it. It needs a separate broker-level benchmark against supabase/functions/delegated-credentials/index.ts.

INF-01/INF-02 scanning is reachable only from the `aidr scan` CLI command (packages/cli/src/commands/scan.ts) and the AIG bridge, not from a connector tool call, so it has no connector x surface combination in this corpus. It needs its own scan-level benchmark.

model-stream is `unsupported` for every sold connector in deploy/native/interception-matrix.json, and residual MKT-03-PROVIDER-STREAM is open: no connector can block provider streaming content before consumption.

No connector intercepts direct (non-tool) host traffic; every `network` row is `unsupported` and residual MKT-03-NETWORK-EGRESS is open. A corpus cannot require prevention on a surface the product does not claim to intercept.

docs/production-readiness/edge-function-contract-manifest.json enumerates the browser-invoked control-plane Edge Functions (identity, billing, policy-management, autosecops-runtime, audit-export and others). They are HTTP control-plane boundaries, not connector interception surfaces, so they belong to a separate control-plane contract benchmark rather than this corpus.
